title: The Sine Rule and the Cosine Rule
seo_title: Sine and Cosine Rules – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Use the sine rule and cosine rule to find sides and angles; find the area of a triangle using ½ab sin C; solve bearing problems. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on the sine rule, the cosine rule, the area ½ab sin C and bearing problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Use the sine rule when you know a side and its opposite angle.
  • Use the cosine rule when you know two sides and the angle between them, or all three sides.
  • Area = ½ab sin C, where C is the angle between sides a and b.

Examples

Example

b = 8, c = 5, A = 60°

a² = 64 + 25 − 80 × 0.5

Answer: a = 7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the sine rule with no opposite pairUse the cosine rule.
Forgetting 2bc cos Aa² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A.
Using the wrong angle in ½ab sin CUse the angle between a and b.

faq.q: When is the sine rule ambiguous?
faq.a: When you are given two sides and a non-included angle.

items.e: Law of Sines: b/sin B = a/sin A. b = 8 × sin 55° ÷ sin 71° = 6.9.

Find θ, where 0° < θ < 180°, if cos θ = −0.6561. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: cos θ is negative, so θ is obtuse. cos−1(−0.6561) = 131.0°.

items.q: cos 37° = 0.7986. What is cos 143°?
items.e: cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ, so cos 143° = −0.7986. Cosines of obtuse angles are negative.

items.q: Which angle has the same sine as 39°?
Find the two angles between 0° and 180° for which sin θ = 0.7314. Give your answers correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: sin−1 0.7314 = 47.0°. Sine is also positive in the second quadrant: 180° − 47.0° = 133.0°. θ = 47.0° or θ = 133.0°.

A triangle has sides 7 cm, 16 cm and 18 cm. Find the largest angle, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 18 cm. cos C = (7² + 16² − 18²) ÷ (2 × 7 × 16) = −0.0848, so C = 94.9°.

items.q: In a park, paths form a triangle PQR. ∠P = 59°, ∠Q = 44° and QR = 61 m. Find PR, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: QR is opposite ∠P and PR is opposite ∠Q. Sine rule: PR ÷ sin 44° = 61 ÷ sin 59°, so PR = 49.4 m.

items.q: In a park, paths form a triangle PQR. ∠P = 46°, ∠Q = 58° and QR = 79 m. Find PR, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: QR is opposite ∠P and PR is opposite ∠Q. Sine rule: PR ÷ sin 58° = 79 ÷ sin 46°, so PR = 93.1 m.

items.q: A ship sails 30 km on a bearing of 070°. How far east of its starting point is it, correct to 1 decimal place?
items.e: The bearing is the angle from north, so the distance east is 30 sin 70° = 28.2 km.

items.q: A boat sails 6 km from A to B on a bearing of 010°, then 13 km from B to C on a bearing of 120°. Find the distance AC, correct to 1 decimal place.

items.q: Yusuf walks 4 km due north and then 14 km due east. Find the bearing of his finishing point from the start, correct to 1 decimal place.
items.e: tan θ = 14 ÷ 4, so θ = 74.1°, measured clockwise from north. The bearing is 074.1° (the distance is 14.6 km).

items.q: Peter walks 12 km due north and then 19 km due east. Find the bearing of his finishing point from the start, correct to 1 decimal place.
